audits.title: Clinic audit on Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) management in public primary care setting: Hong Kong experience
audits.standard: Evidence-based audit criteria and performance standards for COPD care
audits.setting: 73 public primary care clinics, Hospital Authority

cycle1.result: Smokers referred to cessation service 57.6%, attended 50.9%; influenza vaccine 46.9%; pneumococcal vaccine 40.7%; spirometry 19.1%; AECOPD admission 12.8%.

audits.intervention: One-year implementation phase with a series of improvement strategies (not detailed).

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in all criteria; AECOPD admission rate reduced to 9.6%.

audits.citation: Rui Catherine CX, Nga FS, Kit LW, Wing Catherine NS, Yan Wendy KW, Kwong WT, et al.. Clinic audit on Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) management in public primary care setting: Hong Kong experience. . 2020. doi:10.1101/2020.11.26.20239541.

audits.title: Clinical control in COPD and therapeutic implications: The EPOCONSUL audit.

cycle1.result: Control analysed in 1804 (42.7%); 49.1% uncontrolled; therapeutic inertia in 68.4% of uncontrolled patients.

audits.other_findings: 42.2% of patients disagreed with the doctor's reported good control; no action taken for 9.1% of uncontrolled patients.
audits.citation: Calle Rubio M, Miravitlles M, Soler Cataluña JJ, López-Campos JL, Alcázar Navarrete B, Fuentes Ferrer ME, et al.. Clinical control in COPD and therapeutic implications: The EPOCONSUL audit. PLoS One. 2025;20(1):e0314299. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0314299. PMID: 39787174.

audits.title: Accuracy of diagnostic registers and management of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: the Devon primary care audit.
audits.standard: NICE COPD guidelines for diagnosis and treatment
audits.setting: Primary care practices in Devon, visits by a respiratory specialist nurse

cycle1.result: 580 had spirometry; COPD confirmed in 422 (73%); LAMA/SAMA and LABA under-prescribed (indicated but not received in 15-18%); inhaled steroids recommended in 17% but taken by 60%.

audits.other_findings: Reversibility testing changed diagnosis in 11% and severity grading in 18%; three quarters offered smoking cessation help; only 4% with productive cough received mucolytics; pulmonary rehabilitation under-used or unavailable.
audits.citation: Jones RC, Dickson-Spillmann M, Mather MJ, Marks D, Shackell BS. Accuracy of diagnostic registers and management of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: the Devon primary care audit. Respir Res. 2008;9:62. doi:10.1186/1465-9921-9-62. PMID: 18710575.

audits.title: Clinical audit on diagnostic accuracy and management of respiratory failure in COPD.
audits.standard: GOLD 2008 guidelines; accuracy of respiratory failure diagnosis and LTOT prescription

cycle1.result: ABG performed in 118 (90.8%); diagnosis of respiratory failure agreed with ABG in only about half.

audits.other_findings: Treatment adherence to guidelines and LTOT prescription were good.
audits.citation: Menzella F, Facciolongo N, Lusuardi M, Piro R, Formisano D, Castagnetti C, et al.. Clinical audit on diagnostic accuracy and management of respiratory failure in COPD. Respir Care. 2012;57(12):2067-2073. doi:10.4187/respcare.01502. PMID: 22613356.

audits.title: Improving quality of care among COPD outpatients in Denmark 2008-2011.
audits.standard: Recommended processes of COPD care (annual FEV1, BMI, MRC dyspnoea, smoking status, cessation advice, pulmonary rehabilitation)
audits.setting: Danish Clinical Register of COPD, national

cycle1.result: Baseline process indicator fulfilment (figures not given in abstract).

audits.intervention: National multidisciplinary quality improvement programme with register monitoring and audit

cycle2.result: Registration fulfilment above 85% for all indicators; RR vs 2008: FEV1 2.14, BMI 2.24, MRC dyspnoea 2.25, smoking status 2.41, cessation advice 3.40, pulmonary rehabilitation offer 2.78.

audits.other_findings: Moderate variation between regions and clinics persisted in 2011.
audits.citation: Tøttenborg SS, Thomsen RW, Nielsen H, Johnsen SP, Frausing Hansen E, Lange P. Improving quality of care among COPD outpatients in Denmark 2008-2011. Clin Respir J. 2013;7(4):319-327. doi:10.1111/crj.12009. PMID: 23163961.

audits.title: Audit on the appropriateness of integrated COPD management: the "ALT-BPCO" project.
audits.standard: Italian Ministry of Health guidelines on integrated COPD management (COPD-GL)
audits.setting: 29 respiratory units in one Italian region (ALT-BPCO project)

cycle1.result: Mean agreement with recommendations 25% in medical practice and 48% in health organisation.

audits.intervention: Education of respiratory unit specialists on COPD-GL.

cycle2.result: Agreement 60.7% in clinical practice and 54.7% in organisation.

audits.other_findings: Organisational gaps were harder to resolve than gaps in specialist clinical practice.
audits.citation: Nardini S, Cicchitto G, De Benedetto F, Donner CF, Polverino M, Sanguinetti CM, et al.. Audit on the appropriateness of integrated COPD management: the "ALT-BPCO" project. Multidiscip Respir Med. 2014;9(1):40. doi:10.1186/2049-6958-9-40. PMID: 25097757.

audits.title: Guideline Adherence in Outpatient Clinics for Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: Results from a Clinical Audit.
audits.standard: Three COPD guidance documents; performance graded excellent (>80%), good (60-80%), adequate (40-59%), inadequate (20-39%)
audits.setting: 9 hospital outpatient respiratory clinics in Andalusia

cycle1.result: Excellent or good adherence for symptom recording, MRC or CAT use, smoking status, spirometry and bronchodilator therapy.

audits.other_findings: Poor areas: BODE index, treatment monitoring, alpha1-antitrypsin, exercise testing and vaccination advice.

audits.title: Clinical audit of COPD in outpatient respiratory clinics in Spain: the EPOCONSUL study.
audits.standard: Current COPD clinical practice guidelines (Spanish National Guideline for COPD and GOLD)

cycle1.result: 12.1% did not meet diagnostic spirometry criteria; dyspnoea grade assessed in 81.9%, exacerbation history 70.9%, BODE index 12.4%, phenotype 46.3%, GOLD risk 21.9%.

audits.other_findings: Implementation of preventive and educational guideline items was insufficient.

audits.title: Reducing socioeconomic inequalities in COPD care in the hospital outpatient setting - A nationwide initiative.
audits.standard: Six evidence-based national COPD process performance measures
audits.setting: All pulmonary specialised outpatient clinics in Denmark; national quality initiative

cycle1.result: 11% of patients received all relevant care processes.

audits.intervention: Mandatory national quality improvement initiative with regular audits, knowledge sharing and disease-specific recommendations.
audits.other_findings: 23,741 patients 2008-2012; socioeconomic differences seen in 2008 (e.g. immigrants RR 0.41) were eliminated.
audits.citation: Tøttenborg SS, Lange P, Thomsen RW, Nielsen H, Johnsen SP. Reducing socioeconomic inequalities in COPD care in the hospital outpatient setting - A nationwide initiative. Respir Med. 2017;125:19-23. doi:10.1016/j.rmed.2017.02.016. PMID: 28340857.

audits.title: Community Assessment of COPD Health Care (COACH) study: a clinical audit on primary care performance variability in COPD care.
audits.standard: Two national COPD guidelines used as benchmark; adequacy graded excellent (over 80%) to highly inadequate
audits.setting: 63 primary care centres in 6 regions (COACH study)

cycle1.result: Correct diagnosis with spirometric obstruction in 17.6% (9.8 to 23.3% by region); dyspnoea evaluated in 11.1%; 33.6% received no maintenance inhaled therapy.

audits.other_findings: Most parameters were inadequate; best recorded items were exacerbations in the previous year (81.4%) and influenza vaccination (87.7%).
audits.citation: Abad-Arranz M, Moran-Rodríguez A, Mascarós Balaguer E, Quintana Velasco C, Abad Polo L, Núñez Palomo S, et al.. Community Assessment of COPD Health Care (COACH) study: a clinical audit on primary care performance variability in COPD care. BMC Med Res Methodol. 2018;18(1):68. doi:10.1186/s12874-018-0528-4. PMID: 29970023.

audits.setting: Outpatient respiratory clinics in 28 hospitals (EPOCONSUL national audit)

cycle1.result: Clinical control more frequent in specialised than general clinics for non-severe patients (70.5% v 56.1%).

audits.title: An audit of COPD: diagnosis and management in general practice.
audits.setting: Five general practices in Hull and East Riding

cycle1.result: 388 (36%) of 1088 patients on the COPD register had an FEV1/FVC ratio of ≥0.7 (outside the diagnostic range).

audits.other_findings: FEV1 % predicted was a poor indicator of exacerbation frequency; elevated blood eosinophils on at least two occasions was highly predictive of exacerbations.
audits.citation: Hamad G, Rigby A, Morice AH. An audit of COPD: diagnosis and management in general practice. ERJ Open Res. 2020;6(4):330-2020. doi:10.1183/23120541.00330-2020. PMID: 33263022.

audits.title: Clinical Audit on Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) Management in Primary Care: A Quality Improvement Project from Hong Kong.
audits.standard: Six evidence-based audit criteria for COPD care
audits.setting: 73 public primary care clinics, Hospital Authority of Hong Kong

cycle1.result: Of 3102 active smokers, 1788 (57.6%) referred for smoking cessation and 1578 (50.9%) attended; influenza vaccine 4866 (46.9%); pneumococcal vaccine 4227 (40.7%); spirometry 1983 (19.1%); AECOPD admission 1327 (12.8%).

audits.intervention: Series of quality improvement strategies in a one-year implementation phase (systematic team approach)

cycle2.result: All criteria significantly improved, with marked rises in vaccine uptake and spirometry; AECOPD admission rate fell to 9.6%.

audits.citation: Chen XRC, Fu SN, Leung WK, Ng SWC, Kwan WYW, Wong TK, et al.. Clinical Audit on Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) Management in Primary Care: A Quality Improvement Project from Hong Kong. Int J Chron Obstruct Pulmon Dis. 2021;16:1901-1911. doi:10.2147/copd.s304527. PMID: 34188466.

audits.title: Characteristics and actions in high-risk COPD in unstable patients: The EPOCONSUL audit.
audits.setting: Outpatient respiratory clinics in Spain (EPOCONSUL audit)

cycle1.result: 30.1% of high-risk patients unstable; no action taken in 10.1% of unstable patients and no pharmacological change in 56%.

audits.other_findings: Triple therapy prescribed in 68% of unstable patients; 25% on triple therapy also on oral therapy.
audits.citation: Calle Rubio M, Alcázar-Navarrete B, López-Campos JL, Miravitlles M, Soler-Cataluña JJ, Fuentes Ferrer ME, et al.. Characteristics and actions in high-risk COPD in unstable patients: The EPOCONSUL audit. PLoS One. 2025;20(7):e0327775. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0327775. PMID: 40679959.

audits.title: Does Evaluation and Management of COPD Follow Therapeutic Strategy Recommendations?
audits.standard: COPD therapeutic strategy recommendations for symptom and exacerbation risk assessment
audits.setting: Nine pulmonary and 15 primary care physician practices, Southeastern United States

cycle1.result: Clinicians felt 33% of patients had at least 2 exacerbations in the past year versus 56% reported by patients.

audits.intervention: Focused educational peer-to-peer small group webinars based on audit and feedback.

cycle2.result: Improvements in processes of care and outcomes were noted in the year after the intervention.

audits.other_findings: Clinicians' impression of care differed from what patients recalled.
audits.citation: Martinez FJ, Thomashow B, Sapir T, Simone L, Carter J, Han M. Does Evaluation and Management of COPD Follow Therapeutic Strategy Recommendations?. Chronic Obstr Pulm Dis. 2021;8(2):230-242. doi:10.15326/jcopdf.2020.0175. PMID: 33610138.

audits.title: Variations in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Outpatient Care in Respiratory Clinics: Results From the 2021 EPOCONSUL Audit.
audits.standard: Spanish National Guidelines for COPD care (GesEPOC) and GOLD recommendations
audits.setting: Respiratory outpatient clinics, 45 hospitals (EPOCONSUL national audit)

cycle1.result: Alpha-1-antitrypsin serum level testing available in 18.9%

cycle2.result: Alpha-1-antitrypsin testing available in 38.7%; GesEPOC phenotype reported in 63.1%; GOLD assessment in 38.3%

audits.other_findings: Adherence to guideline recommendations improved overall but seemed linked to availability of resources.
audits.citation: Calle Rubio M, López-Campos JL, Miravitlles M, Soler Cataluña JJ, Alcázar Navarrete B, Fuentes Ferrer ME, et al.. Variations in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Outpatient Care in Respiratory Clinics: Results From the 2021 EPOCONSUL Audit. Arch Bronconeumol. 2023;59(5):295-304. doi:10.1016/j.arbres.2023.02.004. PMID: 36858911.
